title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Mining Rights

articles.content_en: Article 1 The People's Court shall, when hearing disputes over mining rights such as prospecting rights and mining rights, protect the transfer of mining rights according to law, maintain market order and transaction security, ensure the rational exploitation and utilization of mineral resources, and promote resource conservation and environmental protection.

Article 2 With respect to a mining rights concession contract entered into between the competent department of land and resources of the people's government at or above the county level as the grantor and the grantee, unless otherwise provided by laws or administrative regulations, if the parties request to confirm that the contract shall take effect from the date it is lawfully established, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 3 If the grantee requests to confirm its prospecting right or mining right from the start date of the validity period specified in the mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit, the People's Court shall support such request.
After the mining rights concession contract takes effect but before the mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit is issued, if a third party conducts illegal exploration or exploitation by crossing boundaries or by other means, and the grantee who has actually occupied the exploration operation area or mining area with the consent of the grantor requests the third party to bear tort liability such as cessation of infringement, removal of obstacles, and compensation for losses, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 4 If the grantor fails to deliver the exploration operation area or mining area, or issue the mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit, in accordance with the concession contract, and the grantee requests dissolution of the concession contract, the People's Court shall support such request.
If the grantee fails to meet the requirements of the mine geological environment protection and restoration plan approved by the competent department of land and resources in its exploration and exploitation of mineral resources, refuses to make corrections within the time limit specified by the competent department of land and resources, or has its mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit revoked due to violation of laws or regulations, or fails to pay the mining rights concession price in accordance with the concession contract, and the grantor requests dissolution of the concession contract, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 5 If a contract is concluded to entrust others with the exploration and exploitation of mineral resources without obtaining a mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit, the People's Court shall, according to law, determine the contract to be void.

Article 6 A mining rights transfer contract shall have legal binding force from the date it is lawfully established. If the application for transfer of mining rights has not been approved by the competent department of land and resources, and the grantee requests the transferor to go through the registration procedures for change of mining rights, the People's Court shall not support such request.
If a party requests to confirm the transfer contract as void solely on the ground that the application for transfer of mining rights has not been approved by the competent department of land and resources, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 7 After a mining rights transfer contract is lawfully established, in the absence of circumstances rendering it void as prescribed by law, if the grantee requests the transferor to perform the obligation of submitting for approval, or the transferor requests the grantee to perform the obligation of assisting with submission for approval, the People's Court shall support such request, unless the conditions for performance are not available in law or in fact.
The People's Court may, based on the facts of the case and the request of the grantee, adjudge that the grantee shall handle the approval procedures on behalf of the transferor, and the transferor shall perform the obligation of assistance and bear the expenses incurred thereby.

Article 8 After a mining rights transfer contract is lawfully established, if the transferor refuses to perform the obligation of submitting for approval without justifiable reasons, and the grantee requests dissolution of the contract, return of the transfer payment paid and interest, and that the transferor shall bear liability for breach of contract, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 9 If a mining rights transfer contract stipulates that the approval procedures shall be handled after the grantee pays all or part of the transfer price, and the transferor requests the grantee to first perform the payment obligation before handling the approval procedures, the People's Court shall support such request, unless the grantee has conclusive evidence proving that there exist circumstances such as the transferor transferring the same mining rights to a third party, or the mining rights holder will be merged or reorganized, which fall under the provisions of Article 68 of the Contract Law.

Article 10 If the competent department of land and resources does not approve the application for transfer of mining rights, resulting in the dissolution of the mining rights transfer contract, and the grantee requests the return of the transfer payment paid and interest, the mining right holder requests the grantee to return the mineral products obtained and the proceeds, or the prospecting right holder requests the grantee to return the exploration data and the mineral products recovered during exploration and the proceeds, the People's Court shall support such requests, provided that the grantee may request a deduction of relevant costs and expenses.
If one party is at fault for the failure to obtain approval for the mining rights transfer application, it shall compensate the other party for the losses suffered thereby; if both parties are at fault, they shall bear corresponding liabilities respectively.

Article 11 After a mining rights transfer contract is lawfully established but before the approval of the competent department of land and resources, if the mining rights holder again transfers the mining rights to a third party and such transfer has been approved and registered by the competent department of land and resources, and the grantee requests dissolution of the transfer contract, return of the transfer payment paid and interest, and that the mining rights holder shall bear liability for breach of contract, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 12 If the parties request to confirm that a mining rights lease or contract for work shall take effect from the date it is lawfully established, the People's Court shall support such request.
If a mining rights lease or contract for work stipulates that the mining rights holder only collects rent or contracting fees, abandons mine management, fails to perform statutory obligations such as production safety and ecological environment restoration, and does not bear corresponding legal liability, the People's Court shall, according to law, determine the contract to be void.

Article 13 With respect to a contract concluded by a mining rights holder with another person for cooperative exploration and exploitation of mineral resources, if the parties request to confirm that the contract shall take effect from the date it is lawfully established, the People's Court shall support such request.
The provisions of this Interpretation on mining rights transfer contracts shall apply to the clauses concerning mining rights transfer in such contract.

Article 14 If a mining rights holder mortgages the mining rights to a creditor to secure the performance of its own debts or the debts of another person, the mortgage contract shall take effect from the date it is lawfully established, unless laws or administrative regulations provide that such mortgage is not allowed.
If a party requests to confirm the mortgage contract as void solely on the ground that it has not been approved, registered or filed with the competent authority, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 15 If a party requests to confirm that the mortgage right over mining rights is established from the time of registration according to law, the People's Court shall support such request.
The mining rights mortgage filing procedures handled by the competent department of land and resources that issues the mineral resources exploration permit or mining permit in accordance with relevant provisions shall be deemed as the registration prescribed in the preceding paragraph.

Article 16 If the debtor fails to perform the due debts or the circumstances agreed by the parties for realizing the mortgage occur, and the mortgagee applies for realizing the mortgage pursuant to Articles 196 and 197 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may auction or sell the mining rights or order that the mining rights be used to offset the debt, provided that the bidder or grantee of the mining rights shall meet the corresponding qualification conditions.

Article 17 If, during the period of mining rights mortgage, the mining rights are wholly or partially lost due to the merger or reorganization of the mortgagor, or the covering of the mineral deposit, or for other reasons, and the mortgagee requests to recover preferentially from the insurance proceeds, indemnities or compensations received by the mortgagor as a result thereof, or to have such sums deposited, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 18 If the parties agree to explore and exploit mineral resources in areas such as nature reserves, scenic spots, key ecological function zones, ecologically sensitive and fragile areas, which violates the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations or harms the environmental public interest, the People's Court shall, according to law, determine the contract to be void.

Article 19 For tort liability disputes arising from cross-boundary exploration and exploitation of mineral resources, if the exploration and exploitation scope approved by the competent department of land and resources overlaps or the boundaries are unclear, the People's Court shall inform the parties to first apply to the competent department of land and resources for resolution.

Article 20 If, due to cross-boundary exploration and exploitation of mineral resources by another person, the mining rights holder requests the infringer to bear tort liability such as cessation of infringement, removal of obstacles, return of property, and compensation for losses, the People's Court shall support such request, except that a prospecting right holder requests the infringer to return the mineral products exploited by cross-boundary exploitation and the proceeds thereof.

Article 21 If exploration and exploitation of mineral resources cause environmental pollution, or result in geological disasters, vegetation damage, or other ecological damage, and the authorities and relevant organizations prescribed by law bring an environmental public interest action, the People's Court shall accept it according to law.
The bringing of an environmental public interest action by the authorities and relevant organizations prescribed by law shall not affect the right of natural persons, legal persons, and other organizations who suffer personal or property damage due to the same exploration and exploitation act to institute an action pursuant to Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 22 If, in hearing a case, the People's Court discovers illegal circumstances such as exploration and exploitation without a permit, falsification of exploration qualifications or geological data, or failure to perform the obligation of ecological environment restoration in exploration and exploitation, it may issue a judicial suggestion to the relevant administrative department, which shall handle it according to law; if the case is suspected of constituting a crime, it shall be transferred to an investigation authority for handling according to law.

Article 23 After this Interpretation comes into force, cases of first instance and second instance that have not yet been concluded by the People's Court shall be governed by the provisions of this Interpretation. For cases where an effective judgment has been made before this Interpretation comes into force, and a retrial is conducted according to law after this Interpretation comes into force, this Interpretation shall not apply.
